description: Two-panel composite figure of room-temperature tensile behaviour of the Fe–30Mn–11Al–1.2C low-density steel at different cold rolling reductions. (a) Engineering stress (MPa, ticks 0–2100 in 300 MPa steps) versus engineering strain (%, 0–100), with eight colour-coded curves listed in a legend: 0% (black), 10% (pale grey-lavender), 20% (navy), 30% (green), 40% (green), 50% (pink), 70% (orange) and 90% (dark red) reduction. Open circles mark the necking point of each sample and are joined by a heavy black dashed line; a bold red arrow labelled 'trade-off' points up-left toward decreasing ductility. (b) True stress (MPa, 0–2100) versus true strain (0.0–0.7) for the same eight conditions, same legend; hollow circles again mark the necking points joined by a dashed black line, and a red arrow annotated 'sharply increase' emphasises the lifted necking true stress at high reduction. In (a) the 0% curve is the weakest but by far the most ductile, while the 90% curve climbs to about the 2100 MPa gridline at very low strain and fractures early. No numeric data labels are printed on any curve.

subfigures.description: Engineering stress (MPa, 0–2100) vs engineering strain (%, 0–100) tensile curves for cold rolling reductions of 0%, 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 70% and 90%, colour-coded in the legend. Hollow circles mark necking points, connected by a heavy black dashed line; a red arrow labelled 'trade-off' points up-left. The 0% curve reaches the largest strain (~85–90%) while the 90% curve peaks at the top of the axis at very low strain.

True stress (MPa, 0–2100) vs true strain (0.0–0.7) for the same eight conditions with the same colour legend. Hollow circles mark the necking points and are joined by a black dashed line that is nearly flat at low-to-medium strain and rises to ~1500 MPa at true strain ≈0.55; a red arrow annotated 'sharply increase' highlights this rise.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is an engineering stress (MPa, axis 0–2100) versus engineering strain (%, axis 0–100) plot containing eight tensile curves labelled by cold rolling reduction: 0%, 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 70% and 90%.
Panel (b) is the corresponding true stress (MPa, axis 0–2100) versus true strain (axis 0.0–0.7) plot for the same eight cold rolling reductions, using the identical colour legend.
In both panels hollow circles mark the necking point of each sample and are connected by a heavy black dashed line ('dark dash lines' in the text).
Panel (a) carries a bold red arrow annotated 'trade-off' pointing up and to the left (toward higher strength / lower ductility); panel (b) carries a red arrow annotated 'sharply increase'.

In (a) the black 0% curve is the lowest in stress but extends furthest in strain (to roughly the 85–90% strain region), while the dark red 90% curve rises steeply to about the 2100 MPa gridline within a few percent strain and then falls/fractures early.
The legend colours map as 0% black, 10% pale grey-lavender, 20% navy, 30% green, 40% green, 50% pink, 70% orange, 90% dark red.
In (b) the dashed line joining the necking points is approximately flat at low-to-medium strain and rises to about the 1500 MPa level at the highest true strain (~0.55).
No numeric data labels are printed on any curve; all values must be read against the axis gridlines.
The caption states that the hollow circle indicates the necking point.
The caption states panel (a) is 'Room-temperature tensile engineering' and panel (b) true stress-strain curves of different cold rolling reduction.
The citing text states the as-quenched steel had YS ~570 MPa and UTS ~830 MPa but a uniform elongation exceeding 75%.
The citing text states YS increased with cold rolling reduction and eventually reached ~2.0 GPa, approximately 3.5 times the as-quenched value.
The citing text states that the true stress at the necking point was similar at low-to-medium rolling reduction (<50%) but was sharply enhanced at higher rolling reductions.
